name: Shai Hulud
label: Revelation
lede: Named for the sandworms in Dune, fronted at first by a fourteen-year-old, and so short on steady singers that they once tried to change their name rather than keep auditioning.

eras.title: Named for a sandworm
eras.text: Pompano Beach, Florida, 1995: a guitarist named Matt Fox and a handful of friends start a band and name it after the giant worms in Frank Herbert's Dune. Within a year they had a Revelation deal, lost their first singer, and replaced him with a ninth-grader.

years.h: Shai Hulud form in Pompano Beach, Florida
years.p: Matt Fox on guitar, Dave Silber on bass, [[Damien Moyal|b655a47c-28f5-466d-aba1-4d607e4f598a]] singing and Jason Lederman on drums. The name is the Fremen word for the sandworms of Arrakis in Frank Herbert's Dune.
years.xp:
The Dune joke runs through everything: the uncredited gang of backing vocalists who turn up on every Shai Hulud record are known as the Fremen Warriors.

Matt Fox has spent decades correcting two assumptions. According to Wikipedia, Shai Hulud has never been a Christian band or a straight edge band; members have included believers and atheists, drinkers and edge kids.

years.h: Shai Hulud's first show: Halloween at Discount's warehouse
years.p: Shai Hulud's first show is on Halloween 1995 at a spot Wikipedia calls Discount's warehouse. Fewer than 50 people came.

years.h: Revelation wants Shai Hulud to change their name
years.p: A six-song demo reaches Revelation, and [[Unbroken|bebbd114-8e34-4035-a66e-37f9c144ca7a]]'s Rob Moran pushes to sign the band. The label's one worry: nobody could remember the name Shai Hulud. The band kept it.
years.xp: Matt Fox told No Echo the demo went to a Revelation staffer named Jeanne, and that Rob Moran of Unbroken is the one who signed them. The records came out on Crisis, Revelation's imprint for heavier bands.

years.h: Damien Moyal leaves; fourteen-year-old Chad Gilbert takes the mic
years.p: Damien Moyal quits Shai Hulud for [[Morning Again|1b4e059e-856e-49a8-b7ca-c3ee67dcde23]], [[Bird of Ill Omen|23fca2fb-72da-4ccb-99b1-5f74652fec0b]] and [[As Friends Rust|2f106f2f-5990-4f50-9590-3fa8da941f98]]. His replacement is [[Chad Gilbert|4ed8c877-0036-44c7-bf6f-4c9c8e8ccedb]], fourteen years old and nearly a decade younger than his bandmates.

years.h: Shai Hulud record A Profound Hatred of Man
years.p: Chad Gilbert's first session with Shai Hulud, with [[Steve Kleisath|faf2720a-5006-412f-8fb6-abef4bb696eb]] of [[Strongarm|039aebd3-83d8-4121-b7ed-5996bbf3518a]] on drums. Kleisath also holds a Mario Bros. arcade world record, over five million points, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: A kid screaming his lungs out
eras.text: Two records in one year on Crisis/Revelation made Shai Hulud's name in hardcore: heavy, melodic, weirdly tender, and sung by a teenager. Then the teenager left to start a pop-punk band that would sell far more records than all of them.

years.h: A Profound Hatred of Man, Shai Hulud's debut EP
years.p: Out on Crisis/Revelation with Chad Gilbert singing. It sets up the formula: metallic riffs, melodic leads and a misanthropic streak Shai Hulud would chase for decades.

q: We didn't know what the hell we were doing
years.h: Hearts Once Nourished with Hope and Compassion
years.p: Recorded at Morrisound in Tampa in August and September 1997. Engineer Steve Heritage marveled that Chad Gilbert was screaming his lungs out; two songs were built from leftover riffs days before the session.
years.xp:
The first 5,000 CDs came out with the band's name misspelled on the spine as Shai Halud. Movie samples from Groundhog Day and Alien are woven between the songs.

Matt Fox has never liked how it sounds. It didn't matter: Loudwire put it on its 2020 list of the 25 best metalcore albums of all time, and bands from [[Poison the Well|5275425d-3cdb-4a9a-b9eb-3e246ec69881]] to [[As I Lay Dying|ba147ea0-60c4-4a40-9da6-0d5c2b2e7b03]] cite it.
play: Hearts Once Nourished with Hope and Compassion
My Heart Bleeds the Darkest Blood

years.h: Chad Gilbert leaves Shai Hulud to start [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]]
years.p: Chad Gilbert quits to form New Found Glory, the Coral Springs pop-punk band that takes him to major-label stardom. He comes back to Shai Hulud more than once.

years.h: Matt Fox and Chad Gilbert start a zombie band
years.p: Their side project Boddicker, later renamed Zombie Apocalypse, writes short thrashy songs about the undead. Its 1998 demo stays unreleased; the first album comes in 2003.

years.h: The Fall of Every Man, split with Indecision
years.p: Three Shai Hulud songs recorded in May 1998, shared with the New York band Indecision. Around it, Shai Hulud tour with [[Strongarm|039aebd3-83d8-4121-b7ed-5996bbf3518a]], [[Bloodlet|754fcd17-fa48-428e-a2cc-f28d314a59e6]], Zao, [[Shadows Fall|2e3b75d8-00a8-486a-b4e7-a1f8f65e64c9]] and even [[Cannibal Corpse|af8e4cc5-ef54-458d-a194-7b210acf638f]].

eras.title: A singer from overseas, a move to Poughkeepsie
eras.text: Almost everyone except Matt Fox changed in 1999. The band found a singer on tour in Europe, moved from Florida to the Hudson Valley, and made a second album that sat on a shelf for a year over its artwork.

years.h: [[Matt Fletcher|bc21c667-3ace-4a25-84db-09c3de31277f]] moves from Oklahoma to join Shai Hulud
years.p: Guitarist Oliver Chapoy leaves and Matt Fletcher relocates to Florida to replace him. Fletcher had first seen Shai Hulud in Seattle in 1997, the night [[Andrew Gormley|32ee6b46-7d6c-4ea4-9b08-2cc64c8ac094]] was selling [[Kiss It Goodbye|f323fac7-b32e-49d5-b0ea-ef66fcf61416]] demos.

years.h: Poison the Well's drummer fills in; Andrew Gormley joins
years.p: Steve Kleisath quits for personal reasons. [[Chris Hornbrook|43c22eda-8673-4347-a431-fa954ecc41ee]] of [[Poison the Well|5275425d-3cdb-4a9a-b9eb-3e246ec69881]] plays a single February show, then Andrew Gormley, ex-[[Rorschach|bfb77d72-8e36-4cf2-be10-7dcdd81d52b4]] and Kiss It Goodbye, takes the kit.

years.h: Geert van der Velde becomes Shai Hulud's singer on a European tour
years.p: Matt Fletcher handles vocals on a European tour until [[Geert van der Velde|0b059231-2886-4338-9b60-c43d7bda2213]], a singer the band met on the road, joins full time. Back in Florida, founding bassist Dave Silber leaves.

years.h: Shai Hulud cover Metallica on Crush 'Em All Vol. 1
years.p: A split with Boy Sets Fire on Undecision Records, with Steve Kleisath back on drums for the one track. The same month brings A Whole New Level of Sickness, a split with Another Victim.

years.h: Shai Hulud leave Florida for Poughkeepsie, New York
years.p: The band relocates from South Florida to Poughkeepsie in the Hudson Valley. Drummers keep rotating: Spikey Goldbach, ex-Inner Dam's Chris Cardinal, then Tony Tintari.

years.h: That Within Blood Ill-Tempered · Revelation
years.p: Produced by Jesse Cannon and finished in May 2002, then held back about a year over artwork disagreements. With no video and no radio, it reached No. 39 on Billboard's Independent Albums chart.
years.xp:
Geert van der Velde's only full-length with the band. He brought the first sung melody to a Shai Hulud album on the opener, Scornful of the Motives. Matt Fox told No Echo the amps hadn't been serviced and needed new tubes before tracking.

A friend, drummer Jay of When Dreams Die, dubbed the sound Legacycore. Fox calls it the record he's proudest of, if not his favorite.

eras.title: The band that almost stopped being Shai Hulud
eras.text: When the singer and drummer walked, Matt Fox and Matt Fletcher decided not to quit. They decided to rename the band instead, and ran open auditions by mail for a new voice.

years.big: New singer, new name: The Warmth of Red Blood
years.h: Shai Hulud announce they'll become The Warmth of Red Blood
years.p: Geert van der Velde and drummer Tony Tintari leave, and guitarist Matt Canning exits for The Twilight Collective. Chad Gilbert fills in for some shows, and the band says it will carry on under a new name.
years.xp: To find a singer, Shai Hulud posted an instrumental of Whether to Cry or Destroy and asked hopefuls to send back their own vocal takes, the same open-call trick [[The Dillinger Escape Plan|1bc41dff-5397-4c53-bb50-469d2c277197]] had used. Lambgoat reported the name change at the time.

years.h: A retrospective of 'Bad and Useless Recordings'
years.p: The full title: A Comprehensive Retrospective: or How We Learned to Stop Worrying and Release Bad and Useless Recordings. Demos and live tracks, co-released by Revelation and the band's own At Dawn We Wage War.

years.h: The Warmth of Red Blood is dropped; Shai Hulud stays Shai Hulud
years.p: After a rough three-song demo with Eric Dellon singing and drumming at once, the band abandons the new name and goes back to Shai Hulud.

years.h: Shai Hulud sign to Metal Blade
years.p: Friends in [[The Black Dahlia Murder|21f3573f-10cf-44b3-aeaa-26cccd8448b5]], [[Unearth|9f336c50-ae4c-4440-bda7-958aa12bc15a]] and [[The Red Chord|d1322057-e047-45ee-a573-769b37a395dc]] had signed there, and Matt Fox wanted to reach past what he saw as a stagnant hardcore scene.

eras.title: Metal Blade, and the kid comes back
eras.text: The first Metal Blade album was built in ProTools and Fox soon called it a misfire. The fix, five years later, was the singer from 1997: Chad Gilbert, now a pop-punk veteran, came back to sing and produce.

years.h: Misanthropy Pure, Shai Hulud's Metal Blade debut
years.p: Matt Mazzali sings and Andrew Gormley drums. The guitars were played slowly and sped up digitally, which Matt Fox later called too perfect and a bit of a misfire. It reached No. 15 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.

years.h: Geert van der Velde returns for Shai Hulud's Japan tour
years.p: Van der Velde steps back in for a February 2009 run through Japan supporting [[Parkway Drive|a436dd02-0549-4c91-b608-df451217fdeb]] and Crystal Lake.

years.h: The split with New Found Glory and the longest title in hardcore
years.p: Not Without a Heart Once Nourished by Sticks and Stones Within Blood Ill-Tempered Misanthropy Pure Gold Can Stay: 500 copies, sold only on New Found Glory's Not Without a Fight tour.

years.h: Shai Hulud play Revelation's 25th anniversary in Pomona
years.p: Shai Hulud join [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]], [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]] and [[Into Another|c235e5fd-4144-4e53-95ff-b33dc5f239c8]] at the Glass House in Pomona, California, for Revelation's 25th birthday.

years.h: Chad Gilbert will produce and sing the next Shai Hulud album
years.p: Matt Fox announces that the band's fourteen-year-old singer from 1996, now New Found Glory's guitarist, is producing and singing the new record.

q: It only took us 4 full-length albums to reach that hallowed place
years.h: Reach Beyond the Sun, sung and produced by Chad Gilbert
years.p: Matt Fox's favorite Shai Hulud record. Fox admits he worried again that Gilbert would lose his voice. Tours include Australia's Soundwave Festival that March.

years.h: Just Can't Hate Enough EP
years.p: A new Shai Hulud EP, with Moe Watson now behind the drums.

eras.title: Singers come and go, then Geert comes home
eras.text: Matt Fox and Matt Fletcher kept the band alive through a run of vocalists. Twenty years after their second album, the band that made it got back on stage together.

years.h: 'Mean' Pete Kowalsky becomes Shai Hulud's singer
years.p: After brief stints by Justin Kraus and Mary Carlock, Pete Kowalsky fronts the band through 2020. [[Jay Pepito|5cfdf41c-fc3c-46cd-96f2-ec4da138c60a]] follows from 2020 to 2024.

years.h: The That Within Blood Ill-Tempered line-up reunites at Furnace Fest
years.p: Geert van der Velde and drummer Tony Tintari rejoin to play the album's 20th anniversary at Furnace Fest, on a bill with [[Poison the Well|5275425d-3cdb-4a9a-b9eb-3e246ec69881]] and [[Underoath|674a7e8c-9682-419a-8e05-2358e28b5359]]. Van der Velde stays on as Shai Hulud's singer.
